name: Seed 2.1 Turbo
tagline: The smaller, faster half of ByteDance's Seed 2.1 family (June 2026) — the same agent-first multimodal recipe as Seed 2.1 Pro at a lower size tier.
seoTitle: Seed 2.1 Turbo — ByteDance's compact Doubao model
metaDescription: Seed 2.1 Turbo: the compact model in ByteDance's Doubao Seed 2.1 family (June 2026), benchmarked by the Seed team against Seed 2.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5.
overview: Seed 2.1 Turbo is the compact model in ByteDance's Doubao Seed 2.1 family, which the Seed team announced on June 23, 2026. ByteDance's Seed 2.1 page presents the generation as 'offering two AI productivity models in different sizes: Pro and Turbo', with Turbo the smaller of the pair and Seed 2.1 Pro the flagship. Like Pro it is served through Volcano Engine rather than released as open weights.

It inherits the generation's agent-first framing: the Seed 2.1 family is pitched at coding engineering delivery, long-chain agent task execution and multimodal understanding rather than single-turn question answering. Turbo is scored across the same published suite as Pro, spanning knowledge, reasoning, office and agent work, coding, terminal use, spatial reasoning and long-video understanding.

On the Seed team's own comparison table Turbo tracks close behind Pro on most rows and ahead of it on a few — BeyondAIMER 88.0 against Pro's 87.0, and Workspace Bench 54.7 against 53.0. It stays competitive on multimodal work (MathVision with tool 92.7, MMMU-Pro with tool 82.2, VideoMME 89.0, MMLongBench-128K 76.9) while giving up ground on the longest-horizon agent rows, where Pro leads by wide margins: Agent Startup Bench 54.0 vs 68.8 and TOMATO 56.8 vs 79.5.

The same table sets both models against Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro. Turbo leads all three on several vision rows — BabyVision 62.9 (best of the group after Pro), WorldVQA 48.6 and ZEROBench with tool 20.0 — while GPT-5.5 remains ahead on most coding and terminal rows. ByteDance publishes no open weights for the Seed line; Turbo's per-token price and context limit are set on Volcano Engine's platform rather than in the Seed team's model page.
strengths: BeyondAIMER 88.0 — above the 87.0 the Seed team reports for the larger Seed 2.1 Pro
Workspace Bench 54.7 for office-style agent work, again ahead of Pro's 53.0
Strong multimodal scores for its size: MathVision with tool 92.7, MMMU-Pro with tool 82.2, CharXiv-RQ with tool 83.6
Long-video and long-context understanding close to Pro — VideoMME 89.0, OVOBench 79.2, MMLongBench-128K 76.9
Same agent-first tuning as Seed 2.1 Pro at a smaller size tier, served through the same Volcano Engine API
useCases: High-volume production traffic where Seed 2.1 Pro's cost per call is the constraint
Multimodal understanding over documents, charts, infographics and video
Coding and terminal agent workflows that do not need Pro's longest-horizon planning
Doubao-based assistants and Volcano Engine applications already targeting the Seed 2.1 generation
